SENTINEL TRAP HIT AND CORRECTED IN THIS RUN'S OWN CHECK SCRIPT, worth recording for future runs. The first cross-check script treated any data-v below 99999 as real and anything else as a sentinel, which silently dropped Beamery's 178010 and AIG's 108910 - both legitimately above 99999 - and made the open-deals table read 107100 against a committed 216010. That was a bug in the check, not a discrepancy in the file. The sentinels are exactly -1 ('not set' amounts) and 99999 ('never' for days-since-last-deal), so a sentinel test must match those two values exactly and never use a magnitude threshold; AIG at 108910 already exceeds the old threshold and the next large deal would too.
